Ocora vol. 2-3 and 4-6 track titles are given in Chinese from the Chinese Wikipedia discography table of 蔡小月, not from the record; the Ocora booklets were not read.
Begin year 1600 is an estimate from the two Ming printed songbooks; their exact dates (often given as 1604 in the van der Loon literature) are not on any page read here.

The English Wikipedia article carries a December 2025 notice that it appears to include language-model text, and its history section calls Quanzhou 廣州 (Guangzhou), an error. Its claims are used only where the Chinese article or UNESCO agree, except the early-20th-century Taiwan peak (60+ associations), which is from that flagged section.

Peaks (CN and TW 1980/1982-2010) are judgements from dated facts (1982 Nansheng She European tour and Ocora series, post-Cultural-Revolution revival, 2006 national list, 2009 UNESCO); no source states a peak.

Release years for iTunes albums come from the releaseDate field of the same lookup pages; they were not recorded as separate claims. 福建南音 (中国地方音乐大系4) is dated 2001 on iTunes, which may be a reissue date.
Rhymoi Music's 2026 album 中国音乐地图之听见福建 福建南音 was found but left out: the performers are not named (artist is the label).
